- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show downward drift or consolidation.
- Forecast exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model may be overweighting recent volatility or ignoring macroeconomic tail risks.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in low-volatility periods — underestimates price drops when market sentiment shifts.
- Model shows lag in adjusting to new information — true values often move faster than forecast, especially in the last 5–10 days.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — spikes in history trigger exaggerated upward forecasts, which then fail to align with subsequent mean-reverting behavior.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy changes or regulatory shifts — when such events occur, true prices drop faster than forecasted.
